facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: Leverage trajectory. Net debt was USD 759.799 million at year-end 2024 and USD 895.779 million at year-end 2025, which is 1.99x and 2.02x reported EBITDA, then USD 2669.704 million at 2026-09-27. The rise of USD 1773.925 million after year-end reflects the July 2026 Ruckus purchase: cash paid for acquisitions was USD 1869.631 million in the nine months, funded by a USD 1,850 million Term Loan B at term SOFR plus 2.25% maturing in 2033, and the rise is smaller than that cost because free cash flow exceeded shareholder payments and the dollar value of the euro notes fell. The January 2026 swap of the 2027 euro notes for new 2033 euro notes was size-neutral and pushed the nearest bond maturity out to 2028, so the maturity wall now sits in 2033 where the term loan and the 2033 notes both fall due. The mechanism for creditors is that the term loan is floating-rate and amortises, so interest cost and mandatory cash outflow both step up while only one quarter of Ruckus earnings is in the trailing figures. facts.text: Contrary evidence and what would change the view. limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- High: no company-stated pro forma net leverage and no Ruckus EBITDA are supplied, so leverage including a full year of Ruckus is not established and the 2026-09-27 trailing ratios overstate it; the action that closes it is the acquisition announcement or a management pro forma. - High: interim cash interest paid is not stated in the 2026 quarterly reports, so interest cover on cash paid is not calculable for 2026-09-27; the action is the interim cash flow supplement or a quarterly interest paid disclosure. - High: covenant terms of the Revolver beyond a fixed charge coverage trigger and all Term Loan B covenants are not supplied, so no headroom is stated and none is inferred; the action is the executed credit agreements. - High: no facility has both a stated legal rank and a stated security, so the debt stack is not drawn; Term Loan B rank and security, the Revolver security and the security of the three euro note issues are left out and the action is the credit agreements and indentures. - Medium: the Ruckus price is stated four ways and the purchase price allocation is preliminary with in-process research and development unvalued, so goodwill of 1000.819 million USD and intangibles of 1040.000 million USD may change; the action is the final allocation. - Medium: the USD cost of repurchasing the 2027 notes is 537.3 million in the annual report and 535.9 million in the 2026 quarterly reports, and the net debt effect of the January and February 2026 refinancing is not stated, so those pro forma rows are not supplied; the action is the refinancing detail. - Medium: Revolver availability of 373.5 million USD is not bridged to the 400.0 million USD commitment and 17.6 million USD of standby letters of credit, and 2024 availability is not stated; the action is the Revolver availability schedule. - Medium: the balance sheets at 2026-03-29 and 2026-06-28 are in the supplied quarterly reports but were not extracted, and no 2025 interim balance sheet is in the sources, so the build-up of net debt before 2026-09-27 and interim comparatives are not shown; the action is to extract the two supplied balance sheets. - Medium: segment disclosure stops after FY2025 because one reportable segment is reported from 2026-01-01, so segment trends cannot continue; the action is a segment bridge from the company. - Low: the filing prints dashes for the loss on debt extinguishment in Q3 2026, the revolver refinancing loss in FY2024, the 2024 borrowing, repayment and debt issuance cost lines and the 2025 current maturities line; each is treated as missing, not zero. - Low: nine-month 2026 cash-flow depreciation and amortization of 146.940 million USD differs from the reconciliation components of 146.470 million USD by 0.470 million USD, and the 2025 figures differ by 0.001 million USD; reported EBITDA uses the components. - Low: capital expenditure is not split between maintenance and growth, noncontrolling interest and per-share data were not extracted, and Q1 and six-month 2026 columns were not extracted although the sources hold them. - Low: lease liabilities, pensions and retiree medical sit outside Total Debt by method and are not added to leverage; operating lease liabilities of 133.727 million USD and finance lease liabilities of 8.525 million USD at 2026-09-27 are named for a reader who wants them. - Low: management assessment of internal control excludes Ruckus for the third quarter, so the acquired balances rest on preliminary purchase accounting and unaudited interim reporting; facts.text: The operating risk sits in a distributor-led channel, where the ten largest customers, eight of them distributors, were 47% of 2025 revenue, and in a newly acquired Ruckus business whose purchase accounting is still preliminary. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Sponsor risk is absent but financial-policy risk has risen. facts.label: Key findings

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is demand and discipline: orders were a record USD 1,017 million in the third quarter, up 16% organically, with a book-to-bill of 1.05x; backlog grew before the deal; the Revolver was repaid within the quarter it was drawn; and earlier acquisitions were funded with cash on hand. A removed leverage goal may reflect wording only. A stated post-deal leverage target, a dated deleveraging plan or a proxy statement showing incentives tied to net debt would move the view toward lower governance risk; a resumed buyback or a larger dividend before leverage falls would move it the other way. facts.label: T2D.9 - Sponsor and governance risk assessment
facts.text: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The level is driven by the debt-funded Ruckus acquisition and the removal of a stated net leverage goal, because they raise leverage tolerance without a creditor-visible limit, which implies higher refinancing pressure and weaker deleveraging visibility. Countervailing evidence is the pause in repurchases, the cash-funded history of earlier acquisitions and an undrawn Revolver. Further analysis requires the proxy statement and the executed credit agreements. facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Belden's credit has weakened materially because the debt-funded Ruckus acquisition lifted net debt to USD 2,669.70 million, or 5.83x trailing reported EBITDA at 2026-09-27, so creditors now depend on earnings growth and free cash flow to deleverage. The business underneath is steady: FY2025 revenue grew 10.33% to USD 2,715.19 million, the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 16.90% and free cash flow was USD 218.88 million. The 5.83x overstates run-rate leverage because only one quarter of Ruckus earnings is in the trailing figures and the company states no pro forma figure, so the true level is not established; on the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA the trailing ratio is 4.79x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C01

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Leverage, not the operating business, is the credit constraint, and it is not yet established on a run-rate basis. Net leverage was 2.02x at year-end 2025 and is 6.25x pro forma for the Ruckus purchase on 2026-07-01, a standalone figure that carries no Ruckus earnings; at 2026-09-27 it is 5.83x on reported and 4.79x on Adjusted trailing EBITDA, and 4.95x after removing USD 17.9 million of tariff refunds on 2025 purchases that the issuer includes in Adjusted EBITDA. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C01; calculation C02

facts.text: - Interest cost is the transmission channel from the acquisition to cash flow. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a negative reading is demand and earnings momentum: orders were a record USD 1,017 million, up 16% organically, the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 17.7%, up 70 bp, and fourth-quarter revenue guidance is USD 960 million to USD 980 million. Because the trailing ratios carry one quarter of Ruckus against its full term loan, true leverage is lower than 4.79x if Ruckus earns at its first-quarter rate before the non-cash charges, and the euro notes are fixed-rate with the nearest maturity in 2028. A company-stated pro forma leverage clearly below the 4.79x trailing figure, voluntary Term Loan B prepayments from free cash flow, or an explicit leverage target would move the view toward improvement; a book-to-bill below 1.00x, an Adjusted EBITDA margin back below 17.0%, or a resumed buyback before leverage falls would deepen it. facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Overall, Belden presents an adequate business profile supported by 11% organic growth, record orders and a 16.90% Adjusted EBITDA margin, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 5.83x trailing reported EBITDA after the debt-funded Ruckus acquisition. Cash-flow durability appears adequate before the deal and less certain after it, because free cash flow conversion fell to 24.69% of Adjusted EBITDA in the nine months of 2026 and coupon interest is about USD 158.69 million a year. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on leverage falling before the 2028 notes and the 2033 maturity wall. The primary downside path is distributor destocking or a reversal of tariff relief that cuts earnings while floating-rate interest stays high. Further analysis would require company pro forma EBITDA, interim cash interest and the credit agreements. Top risk: leverage that does not fall because Ruckus earns too little. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C04

facts.label: Company description and credit linkage
facts.text: Belden supplies network infrastructure (copper and fiber cable, connectivity, racks and enclosures) and industrial networking and automation products, and since 2026-07-01 wireless and cloud-managed networking through Ruckus. Revenue is mostly short-cycle product sales through distributors and OEMs, 42% of 2025 sales were outside the United States, and the 2025 backlog of USD 567.7 million equals 20.91% of revenue, so cash flow is visible for months rather than years. That supports debt service in a normal year but gives little contractual cover in a downturn, which is why leverage matters more than for a contracted-revenue issuer. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is driven by volume and by copper pass-through pricing, and it is concentrated in a distributor channel with no contractual minimums: the ten largest customers were 47% of 2025 revenue, eight of them distributors, and the largest was 14%. Pricing power is limited because markets are described as highly competitive with a 5% to 15% market share, so margin is defended by mix and product breadth rather than price. The implication is that a destocking quarter at a few distributors would cut revenue before the cost base can adjust, which is the first break in the downside path. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Gross margin was 37.98% in FY2025 and, because copper costs reach cost of sales about two months after price moves and OEM contracts pass cost through with a lag of up to three months, margin moves with copper in short windows. The 2026 margin figures are distorted by Ruckus: the Q3 gross margin of 35.07% includes USD 56.3 million of inventory step-up, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin of 17.7% includes tariff refunds the quarterly report names as a driver of margin expansion. Pass-through defends margin against input-cost moves but not against lost volume, and the 2026 improvement is partly one-off, so the run-rate level is lower than the reported rise. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is intense and fragmented, which caps pricing and means share gains come from product breadth and acquisitions rather than price. Buyer power is high because the ten largest customers are 47% of revenue and customers are not obliged to buy minimum amounts, so a few distributors can reshape volumes. Supplier power is moderate: copper is the principal input, its 2025 spot price ranged from USD 3.99 to USD 5.80 a pound, and the company does not generally hedge it with derivatives. Entry barriers and substitution are not quantified in the filings, so they carry no weight in the conclusion. facts.text: Scale is average to strong: revenue of USD 2,715.19 million in FY2025 and USD 3,132.61 million over the last twelve months, but a 5% to 15% market share. Cost and capex flexibility is average because capex of 5.51% of revenue is not split. Margin stability is average, supported by copper pass-through but flattered by tariff refunds in 2026. Free cash flow stability is average and weakening, with conversion at 24.69% in the nine months of 2026. Access to capital markets is average: the Revolver and notes are in place, but no rating is supplied and 72.40% of principal falls due in 2033. Liquidity is average to strong at USD 754.21 million with little principal due before 2028, and financial policy and governance are average: no sponsor and paused buybacks, but a removed leverage goal. The supports are earnings momentum and liquidity, the constraints are leverage and interest cost, the trend is weaker than FY2025, and the missing data are pro forma EBITDA, interim cash interest and the credit agreements. Access to capital markets is average: the Revolver and notes are in place, but no rating is supplied and 72.40% of principal falls due in 2033. Liquidity is average to strong at USD 754.21 million with little principal due before 2028, and financial policy and governance are average: no sponsor and paused buybacks, but a removed leverage goal. The supports are earnings momentum and liquidity, the constraints are leverage and interest cost, the trend is weaker than FY2025, and the missing data are pro forma EBITDA, interim cash interest and the credit agreements.

facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months demand supports the credit: orders are at record levels entering the fourth quarter, guidance is USD 960 million to USD 980 million of revenue, and the data center agreement adds USD 100 million in 2027. Headwinds are the integration of Ruckus, the unwinding of tariff refunds, floating-rate interest and the sharp rise in non-cash charges that depress reported earnings. Over three to five years the 2028, 2031 and 2033 maturities and the Term Loan B balance of USD 1,734.38 million due in 2033 require leverage to fall, which management's goal of mid-single-digit growth and 25% to 30% incremental margins would support if met. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario starts with distributors cutting inventory as demand slows while tariff refunds stop. Revenue falls first because the backlog of USD 567.7 million is short-cycle; gross margin follows because copper costs lag price by about two months; Adjusted EBITDA falls faster than revenue because operating costs and Ruckus integration spending do not adjust quickly. On the trailing base of USD 557.17 million, a 10% fall in Adjusted EBITDA lifts leverage to 5.32x and a 20% fall to 5.99x with no change in net debt, while coupon cover drops to 2.81x. Free cash flow shrinks toward the interest bill, so the Revolver is likely to be drawn first, but USD 754.21 million of liquidity and a nearest maturity in 2028 mean liquidity distress is not the likely outcome inside 24 months; management levers are capex cuts, a continued buyback pause and working capital release. The observable triggers are book-to-bill below 1.00x, margin below 17.0% and Revolver availability moving toward USD 27.0 million. ## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and releases are enough for a credit snapshot of Belden at year-end 2025 and through the third quarter of 2026, but creditors cannot verify covenant terms, security or ratings because no credit agreement, indenture or rating report was supplied.

The year-end 2025 balance sheet is no guide to current debt: the Ruckus Networks acquisition closed on July 1, 2026 and was funded by a new term loan, purchase accounting is still preliminary and no company-stated net leverage for the enlarged group was supplied. Work on debt, liquidity and earnings can proceed from the filings, while covenant, recovery and security conclusions cannot be drawn until the agreements are supplied.

## Request

Financial foundation for BELDEN INC. (bdc), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway (credit_snapshot). Scope: audited FY2025 and FY2024 statements and the unaudited 2026 interim statements to 2026-09-27 in USD, carrying-value debt, leverage, cash interest cover, liquidity, maturities and dated events after the year-end.

| EX-99.1_2026-07-30_companynewsreleasedatedjul.htm.jsonl | Exhibit 99.1 earnings release for the second quarter of 2026 | 2026-07-30 | 97518bcedf20ecd151c6170017340147f2d2133733fbcb29ebcfd34f2604e982 | Q2 2026 orders, book-to-bill, margin and organic growth for the KPI dashboard. |

## Findings
### Bottom line

Belden's net leverage was 2.02x at year-end 2025 but reached 5.83x on last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at September 2026, because the July 2026 Ruckus Networks acquisition added a debt-funded term loan, so creditors should treat the year-end figures as superseded.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 11–13; calculation C03; calculation C05; calculation C12

The 5.83x overstates the run-rate position because only one quarter of Ruckus earnings is in the denominator while the full USD 1,850 million term loan is in the debt; on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA the same measure is 4.79x, and the company states no pro forma EBITDA or leverage. Interest cover was 10.26x on cash interest paid in FY2025, but no interim cash interest figure is stated.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 17–20; 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 107; Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C05; calculation C12
### Financial interpretation

Leverage trajectory. Net debt was USD 759.799 million at year-end 2024 and USD 895.779 million at year-end 2025, which is 1.99x and 2.02x reported EBITDA, then USD 2669.704 million at 2026-09-27. The rise of USD 1773.925 million after year-end reflects the July 2026 Ruckus purchase: cash paid for acquisitions was USD 1869.631 million in the nine months, funded by a USD 1,850 million Term Loan B at term SOFR plus 2.25% maturing in 2033, and the rise is smaller than that cost because free cash flow exceeded shareholder payments and the dollar value of the euro notes fell. The January 2026 swap of the 2027 euro notes for new 2033 euro notes was size-neutral and pushed the nearest bond maturity out to 2028, so the maturity wall now sits in 2033 where the term loan and the 2033 notes both fall due. The mechanism for creditors is that the term loan is floating-rate and amortises, so interest cost and mandatory cash outflow both step up while only one quarter of Ruckus earnings is in the trailing figures.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 11–13; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 93; calculation C03; calculation C14

Coverage. Cash interest paid was USD 43.157 million in FY2025 and USD 42.402 million in FY2024, giving reported EBITDA cover of 10.26x and 9.01x. The 2026 quarterly reports do not state interest paid, so interim cash cover is not established. On the accrual measure, Q3 2026 net interest expense was USD 41.802 million against USD 11.562 million a year earlier, and Q3 2026 reported EBITDA covered it 2.25x (4.09x on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA); the Q3 reported figure carries USD 56.3 million of non-cash inventory fair-value step-up that the issuer adds back.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C04; calculation C13

Cash-flow quality. Operating cash flow was USD 240.200 million in the nine months of 2026 against USD 194.476 million a year earlier, and issuer-defined free cash flow was USD 107.444 million against USD 97.610 million; FY2025 free cash flow of USD 218.883 million was 0.49 of reported EBITDA. Receivables absorbed USD 79.039 million in the nine months while payables and accrued liabilities supplied USD 45.592 million, so working capital was a net use of cash despite a favourable payables swing, and the 2026 operating cash flow carries only one quarter of Ruckus.

Liquidity. Cash was USD 380.706 million at 2026-09-27, of which USD 232.0 million was held outside the United States, and the Revolver had USD 373.5 million of stated availability against a USD 400.0 million commitment; the Revolver was drawn USD 50.0 million on 2026-06-29 and repaid on 2026-09-25, so quarter-end availability understates intra-quarter use. Term Loan B current maturities are USD 18.500 million. Availability is not bridged to the commitment or to the USD 17.6 million of standby letters of credit, and the filing does not say which limit binds.

Non-debt funding float. Deferred revenue rose from USD 49.728 million at January 1, 2026 to USD 250.607 million at 2026-09-27, of which USD 201.675 million came with the Ruckus acquisition and USD 114.9 million is long-term. It is working-capital float that funds operations through customer prepayment, is not debt and is excluded from net debt, and it unwinds as support and software services are delivered rather than as cash is repaid; the acquired balance sits inside purchase accounting that is still preliminary and may change.

Subsequent events. After year-end 2025 three dated events changed the debt structure: the 2033 notes were issued on 2026-01-28, the 2027 notes were repurchased on 2026-02-11 and Ruckus was acquired with Term Loan B on 2026-07-01. They are reflected in the 2026-09-27 balance sheet and are kept out of the year-end 2025 figures, which is why a year-end net debt must be read with the pro forma row. Standing alone, the Ruckus purchase would lift year-end 2025 net debt to USD 2765.410 million, or 6.25x reported FY2025 EBITDA, a figure that excludes any Ruckus earnings and so overstates leverage. No event after 2026-09-27 that changes net debt was found up to the 2026-11-05 cutoff.

Contrary evidence and what would change the view. Orders reached a record USD 1,017 million in Q3 2026 with 11% organic revenue growth, the Revolver was undrawn at quarter-end and adjusted EBITDA margin was 17.7%, which argues for faster deleveraging than the trailing ratio implies. A company-stated pro forma EBITDA that includes a full year of Ruckus, or interim cash interest, would replace the overstated trailing measures with a figure that can be relied on; until then the 4.79x and 5.83x trailing ratios and the 6.25x year-end figure all overstate leverage on a full-year basis, and the answer lies below them.

Data quality and definitions. The issuer states only an adjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is built from net income, tax, net interest and the three depreciation and amortization lines of the issuer's own reconciliation; the nine-month 2026 cash-flow depreciation and amortization differs from those lines by USD 0.470 million. Debt is the balance-sheet carrying value of USD 3,050.410 million, which is USD 53.370 million below the USD 3,103.780 million principal even though one filing paragraph calls the principal a carrying value. Two multi-figure events are logged rather than reconciled: the USD cost of repurchasing the 2027 notes (537.3 in the annual report, 535.9 in the 2026 quarterly reports) and the Ruckus price (four statements between USD 1.846 billion and USD 1,869.6 million net of cash acquired).

- High: no company-stated pro forma net leverage and no Ruckus EBITDA are supplied, so leverage including a full year of Ruckus is not established and the 2026-09-27 trailing ratios overstate it; the action that closes it is the acquisition announcement or a management pro forma.

- High: interim cash interest paid is not stated in the 2026 quarterly reports, so interest cover on cash paid is not calculable for 2026-09-27; the action is the interim cash flow supplement or a quarterly interest paid disclosure.

- High: covenant terms of the Revolver beyond a fixed charge coverage trigger and all Term Loan B covenants are not supplied, so no headroom is stated and none is inferred; the action is the executed credit agreements.

- High: no facility has both a stated legal rank and a stated security, so the debt stack is not drawn; Term Loan B rank and security, the Revolver security and the security of the three euro note issues are left out and the action is the credit agreements and indentures.

- Medium: the Ruckus price is stated four ways and the purchase price allocation is preliminary with in-process research and development unvalued, so goodwill of 1000.819 million USD and intangibles of 1040.000 million USD may change; the action is the final allocation.

- Medium: the USD cost of repurchasing the 2027 notes is 537.3 million in the annual report and 535.9 million in the 2026 quarterly reports, and the net debt effect of the January and February 2026 refinancing is not stated, so those pro forma rows are not supplied; the action is the refinancing detail.

- Medium: Revolver availability of 373.5 million USD is not bridged to the 400.0 million USD commitment and 17.6 million USD of standby letters of credit, and 2024 availability is not stated; the action is the Revolver availability schedule.

- Medium: the balance sheets at 2026-03-29 and 2026-06-28 are in the supplied quarterly reports but were not extracted, and no 2025 interim balance sheet is in the sources, so the build-up of net debt before 2026-09-27 and interim comparatives are not shown; the action is to extract the two supplied balance sheets.
- Medium: segment disclosure stops after FY2025 because one reportable segment is reported from 2026-01-01, so segment trends cannot continue; the action is a segment bridge from the company.

- Low: the filing prints dashes for the loss on debt extinguishment in Q3 2026, the revolver refinancing loss in FY2024, the 2024 borrowing, repayment and debt issuance cost lines and the 2025 current maturities line; each is treated as missing, not zero.

- Low: nine-month 2026 cash-flow depreciation and amortization of 146.940 million USD differs from the reconciliation components of 146.470 million USD by 0.470 million USD, and the 2025 figures differ by 0.001 million USD; reported EBITDA uses the components.

- Low: capital expenditure is not split between maintenance and growth, noncontrolling interest and per-share data were not extracted, and Q1 and six-month 2026 columns were not extracted although the sources hold them.

- Low: lease liabilities, pensions and retiree medical sit outside Total Debt by method and are not added to leverage; operating lease liabilities of 133.727 million USD and finance lease liabilities of 8.525 million USD at 2026-09-27 are named for a reader who wants them.

- Low: management assessment of internal control excludes Ruckus for the third quarter, so the acquired balances rest on preliminary purchase accounting and unaudited interim reporting; no action closes this before the annual report.

## Request

Business and governance fact pack for BELDEN INC. (bdc), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway (credit_snapshot). Scope: transaction, business, ownership, operating model, issuer history and governance and financial-policy behavior from the supplied filings and releases; no sponsor or private equity owner is named in them.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Belden is a listed manufacturer with no sponsor or controlling holder named in its filings, so creditors rely on management's own financial policy, and the filings after the debt-funded Ruckus acquisition no longer state the net leverage goal of about 1.5x.

The operating risk sits in a distributor-led channel, where the ten largest customers, eight of them distributors, were 47% of 2025 revenue, and in a newly acquired Ruckus business whose purchase accounting is still preliminary. Management funded the acquisition with a USD 1,850.0 million term loan and has not repurchased shares since the first quarter, which is consistent with debt reduction but is not a stated policy.
### Key findings

- Sponsor risk is absent but financial-policy risk has risen. The filings name no sponsor, fund or controlling holder, so there is no documented extraction pathway; the exposure is instead management's willingness to hold the balance sheet after a debt-funded purchase, and the documents give no replacement for the 1.5x net leverage goal that the annual report and the first-quarter report printed and the later reports omit.

- The Ruckus acquisition changes the credit more than any other fact. Belden agreed it on 2026-04-29 for about USD 1.85 billion, closed on 2026-07-01, paid USD 1,869.6 million net of cash acquired and funded it with the term loan, so the new loan alone is larger than all the senior subordinated notes outstanding at the start of the year, while the allocation of the price, including in-process research and development, is unfinished, the business lost USD 63.1 million before tax in the quarter and the internal control assessment excludes it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-29_bdc-20260329.htm.jsonl, page 16; EX-99.1_2026-04-30_companynewsreleasedatedmar.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 12, 13, 17, 35

- Repurchases were large against free cash flow before the deal and have paused since. Cash paid under the repurchase program was 89.36% of 2025 free cash flow as the issuer defines it, dividends stayed at USD 0.05 per share a quarter, and no shares were repurchased in the second or third quarter of 2026 with USD 115.0 million of authorization remaining.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 22; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_companynewsreleasedatedoct.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C08

- Revenue is concentrated in channel partners and commodity-linked pricing. The largest distributor was 14% of 2025 revenue, copper price changes reach cost of sales about two months late, and tariff refunds of USD 17.9 million on 2025 transactions reduced the nine-month 2026 cost of sales, so reported margins carry one-offs that need separating.

- The Ruckus balance sheet brings a funding float that is not debt. Deferred revenue rose to USD 250.61 million from USD 49.73 million at the start of 2026, USD 201.68 million of it acquired, so part of the cash flowing through the combined company is customer prepayment for services still to be delivered.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C11
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is demand and discipline: orders were a record USD 1,017 million in the third quarter, up 16% organically, with a book-to-bill of 1.05x; backlog grew before the deal; the Revolver was repaid within the quarter it was drawn; and earlier acquisitions were funded with cash on hand. A removed leverage goal may reflect wording only. A stated post-deal leverage target, a dated deleveraging plan or a proxy statement showing incentives tied to net debt would move the view toward lower governance risk; a resumed buyback or a larger dividend before leverage falls would move it the other way.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_companynewsreleasedatedoct.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 77, 80
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so ownership above 5%, board independence, related-party dealings and incentive metrics are not established, and the view that no controlling holder exists rests on what the filings omit.

- The executed credit agreements are not supplied, so legal capacity for distributions, debt and asset transfers is not assessed and capacity cannot be separated from willingness, which holds the governance level at medium rather than low.

- No Ruckus synergy case, earnings before one-off items or customer data is supplied, so how much of the operating model now depends on Ruckus is shown only by its USD 167.8 million of third-quarter revenue, a USD 63.1 million loss before tax and pro forma revenue and net income.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The loan is floating-rate at term SOFR plus 2.25%, amortizes 0.25% a quarter and matures on 2033-07-01, so creditors hold a much larger and more rate-sensitive structure than the year-end 2025 one.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-30_companynewsreleasedatedmar.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-03-29_bdc-20260329.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 20

The financing amounts are not reconciled in the filings: the cost of repurchasing the 2027 notes appears as 537.3 million USD in the annual report and 535.9 million USD in the 2026 quarterly reports, and the Ruckus price is stated four different ways. spans.text: # CP-2 fundamental credit for BELDEN INC. (bdc)
## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for BELDEN INC. (bdc), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway (credit_snapshot). Scope: business and operating model, cash-flow durability, leverage, liquidity, refinancing capacity, financial policy and the main downside path from the supplied filings, releases and the three earlier analyses; no rating, legal-capacity conclusion, recovery waterfall or position size is given.
## Sources

No external sources were used. Document dates are the signature or release dates the documents state.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Belden's credit has weakened materially because the debt-funded Ruckus acquisition lifted net debt to USD 2,669.70 million, or 5.83x trailing reported EBITDA at 2026-09-27, so creditors now depend on earnings growth and free cash flow to deleverage.

The business underneath is steady: FY2025 revenue grew 10.33% to USD 2,715.19 million, the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 16.90% and free cash flow was USD 218.88 million. The 5.83x overstates run-rate leverage because only one quarter of Ruckus earnings is in the trailing figures and the company states no pro forma figure, so the true level is not established; on the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA the trailing ratio is 4.79x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C01
### Key findings

- Leverage, not the operating business, is the credit constraint, and it is not yet established on a run-rate basis. Net leverage was 2.02x at year-end 2025 and is 6.25x pro forma for the Ruckus purchase on 2026-07-01, a standalone figure that carries no Ruckus earnings; at 2026-09-27 it is 5.83x on reported and 4.79x on Adjusted trailing EBITDA, and 4.95x after removing USD 17.9 million of tariff refunds on 2025 purchases that the issuer includes in Adjusted EBITDA.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C01; calculation C02

- Interest cost is the transmission channel from the acquisition to cash flow. At the 2026-09-27 balances the debt carries about USD 158.69 million of annual coupon interest against USD 46.36 million of net interest expense in FY2025, and trailing Adjusted EBITDA covers that coupon 3.51x. Term Loan B is floating at an average 5.94%, no hedge is stated, so each 100 bp adds USD 18.50 million a year.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 56; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C03

- Cash generation is adequate but converts less of earnings than before the deal. FY2025 free cash flow was 47.71% of Adjusted EBITDA, while the nine months of 2026 converted 24.69% against 28.99% a year earlier as capital spending rose to 5.51% of revenue from 4.86% and integration costs rose; the improvement in operating cash flow came from payables and accrued liabilities rather than earnings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 32; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C04

- Liquidity is adequate for the next two years but is lower in quality than the headline. Cash of USD 380.71 million plus USD 373.50 million of Revolver availability gives USD 754.21 million, which covers the 2028 maturities 1.81x, yet 60.94% of cash is held outside the United States and a fixed charge coverage test applies if availability falls below USD 27.0 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C06

- Refinancing risk is back-ended but heavy. 72.40% of principal falls due in 2033 (the Term Loan B balance and the 2033 notes) and 13.45% in 2028, so refinancing capacity depends on leverage falling before those windows; no rating is supplied and the filings state neither rank nor security for Term Loan B.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C05

- Business quality is average, not strong. Q3 revenue grew 11% organically and orders were a record USD 1,017 million, but the ten largest customers were 47% of 2025 revenue, the largest alone 14%, and copper moves reach cost of sales about two months late; Q3 gross margin was 35.07% against 37.70% a year earlier, and a USD 56.3 million non-cash inventory step-up in cost of sales is part of the fall.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_companynewsreleasedatedoct.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C07

- Ruckus integration is the main execution risk. Ruckus lost USD 63.10 million before tax in its first quarter, after USD 100.0 million of non-cash charges; its goodwill and intangibles total USD 2,040.82 million on preliminary values; and the sources state no synergy figure.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 13; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_companynewsreleasedatedoct.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C11

- Financial policy supports deleveraging in practice but not in stated terms. Shareholder payments of USD 37.68 million in the nine months of 2026 were 35.07% of free cash flow, against repurchases alone of 89.36% in 2025, no shares were repurchased after the first quarter, and the long-term net leverage goal of about 1.5x no longer appears in the reports issued after the acquisition closed.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-06-28_bdc-20260628.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 37; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C12
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a negative reading is demand and earnings momentum: orders were a record USD 1,017 million, up 16% organically, the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 17.7%, up 70 bp, and fourth-quarter revenue guidance is USD 960 million to USD 980 million. Because the trailing ratios carry one quarter of Ruckus against its full term loan, true leverage is lower than 4.79x if Ruckus earns at its first-quarter rate before the non-cash charges, and the euro notes are fixed-rate with the nearest maturity in 2028. A company-stated pro forma leverage clearly below the 4.79x trailing figure, voluntary Term Loan B prepayments from free cash flow, or an explicit leverage target would move the view toward improvement; a book-to-bill below 1.00x, an Adjusted EBITDA margin back below 17.0%, or a resumed buyback before leverage falls would deepen it.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_companynewsreleasedatedoct.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_companynewsreleasedatedoct.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C01
### Limitations
- Pro forma earnings for a full year of Ruckus are not stated, so the leverage conclusion is a range from 4.79x to 5.83x that this analysis cannot narrow, and a lower run-rate level is possible.

- The Term Loan B and Revolver covenant packages are not supplied, so the liquidity and refinancing conclusions assume no restriction beyond the Revolver's fixed charge test and carry no covenant headroom estimate.

- No rating agency view, market pricing or interim cash interest is supplied, so refinancing capacity is not tested against market access and interest cover is measured on coupons and accruals, not cash paid.
- The sources give no end-market or customer revenue split and no Ruckus customer data, so the diversification judgement rests on channel and geography alone.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 35
### Credit view

Overall, Belden presents an adequate business profile supported by 11% organic growth, record orders and a 16.90% Adjusted EBITDA margin, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 5.83x trailing reported EBITDA after the debt-funded Ruckus acquisition. Cash-flow durability appears adequate before the deal and less certain after it, because free cash flow conversion fell to 24.69% of Adjusted EBITDA in the nine months of 2026 and coupon interest is about USD 158.69 million a year. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on leverage falling before the 2028 notes and the 2033 maturity wall. The primary downside path is distributor destocking or a reversal of tariff relief that cuts earnings while floating-rate interest stays high. Further analysis would require company pro forma EBITDA, interim cash interest and the credit agreements. Top risk: leverage that does not fall because Ruckus earns too little.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C04
### Strengths and weaknesses

The main strengths are earnings momentum, near-term liquidity and a cash-funded acquisition record. Orders were a record USD 1,017 million with a book-to-bill of 1.05x and organic growth of 11%, which supports revenue and cash flow over the next year; the nearest bond maturity is 2028 and the Revolver, undrawn at quarter-end, runs to 2030, so no liquidity event arises before leverage can start to fall; and four earlier acquisitions were paid in cash, so the 2026 purchase is the first to be debt-funded.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_companynewsreleasedatedoct.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 80; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The main weaknesses are leverage, interest burden and channel concentration. Net debt of USD 2,669.70 million is 5.83x trailing reported EBITDA and the coupon of about USD 158.69 million is 3.42x the FY2025 net interest expense, which weakens debt service and leaves less room for a downturn; the ten largest customers, eight of them distributors, hold 47% of revenue, so inventory decisions by a few buyers move revenue and margin quickly; and Ruckus lost money in its first quarter on preliminary accounting, so a fall in leverage cannot be confirmed.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C01; calculation C03

| Ruckus purchase | Paid in cash, funded by the term loan | Documentary Fact | Term Loan B | Q3 10-Q: USD 1,850.0 million loan on 2026-07-01 |

| Adjusted EBITDA | Divides net debt to set trailing leverage | Documentary Fact | Net leverage | Q3 10-Q reconciliation; one Ruckus quarter only |
| Liquidity | Cash plus Revolver covers the 2028 maturities | Analyst Interpretation | Refinancing capacity | Q3 10-Q: availability USD 373.5 million |
| Financial policy | Buybacks paused; leverage goal not restated | Documentary Fact | Net leverage | Q3 10-Q: no repurchases in Q2 or Q3 |
| Ruckus earnings | Pro forma EBITDA is not stated | Insufficient Information | Net leverage | Q3 10-Q gives only pro forma revenue and income |
### Company description and credit linkage

Belden supplies network infrastructure (copper and fiber cable, connectivity, racks and enclosures) and industrial networking and automation products, and since 2026-07-01 wireless and cloud-managed networking through Ruckus. Revenue is mostly short-cycle product sales through distributors and OEMs, 42% of 2025 sales were outside the United States, and the 2025 backlog of USD 567.7 million equals 20.91% of revenue, so cash flow is visible for months rather than years. That supports debt service in a normal year but gives little contractual cover in a downturn, which is why leverage matters more than for a contracted-revenue issuer.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C08
### Ownership and group structure

Belden is a listed company with no sponsor or controlling holder named in the supplied filings, so no outside owner is documented to inject equity or extract cash, and its creditors rely on management's own policy. The euro notes, USD 1,253.78 million in total, are issued by Belden Inc., guaranteed on a senior subordinated basis by domestic subsidiaries and subordinated to the Revolver and all other senior debt. The rank and security of the USD 1,850.00 million Term Loan B are not stated, so how much debt ranks ahead of the notes is not established and priority of claim is left for the legal analysis.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C05
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is driven by volume and by copper pass-through pricing, and it is concentrated in a distributor channel with no contractual minimums: the ten largest customers were 47% of 2025 revenue, eight of them distributors, and the largest was 14%. Pricing power is limited because markets are described as highly competitive with a 5% to 15% market share, so margin is defended by mix and product breadth rather than price. The implication is that a destocking quarter at a few distributors would cut revenue before the cost base can adjust, which is the first break in the downside path.
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Gross margin was 37.98% in FY2025 and, because copper costs reach cost of sales about two months after price moves and OEM contracts pass cost through with a lag of up to three months, margin moves with copper in short windows. The 2026 margin figures are distorted by Ruckus: the Q3 gross margin of 35.07% includes USD 56.3 million of inventory step-up, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin of 17.7% includes tariff refunds the quarterly report names as a driver of margin expansion. Pass-through defends margin against input-cost moves but not against lost volume, and the 2026 improvement is partly one-off, so the run-rate level is lower than the reported rise.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 31; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_companynewsreleasedatedoct.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C07
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital expenditure was USD 136.17 million in FY2025, 5.02% of revenue, and rose to 5.51% of revenue in the nine months of 2026; the filings do not split maintenance from growth spending, so flexibility to cut it in a downturn is not established. Free cash flow was 47.71% of Adjusted EBITDA in FY2025 against a management goal of a free cash flow margin approaching 10%, and the FY2025 margin was 8.06%. Severance, restructuring and integration costs of USD 36.70 million in the nine months and the new interest burden will absorb cash that earlier funded buybacks, so debt reduction depends on working capital holding and earnings rising.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 32; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C04
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is intense and fragmented, which caps pricing and means share gains come from product breadth and acquisitions rather than price. Buyer power is high because the ten largest customers are 47% of revenue and customers are not obliged to buy minimum amounts, so a few distributors can reshape volumes. Supplier power is moderate: copper is the principal input, its 2025 spot price ranged from USD 3.99 to USD 5.80 a pound, and the company does not generally hedge it with derivatives. Entry barriers and substitution are not quantified in the filings, so they carry no weight in the conclusion.
### Macro, policy and technology factors

Trade policy and technology matter to credit. Tariffs raised input costs, and refunds of USD 17.9 million on 2025 purchases reduced cost of sales in 2026, so a reversal or new tariffs would lower margin; 40% of Q3 revenue was outside the United States and the euro notes hedge euro net investments, so currency moves the reported debt in dollars, and the dollar carrying value of the 2028 and 2031 notes was lower at 2026-09-27 than at year-end 2025. Data center and automation demand is a tailwind, with a USD 100 million fiber supply agreement for 2027, but it is management language and is not yet in reported results.

### Strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats
- Strengths: record orders, 11% organic growth, a 16.90% Adjusted EBITDA margin, cash-funded earlier acquisitions and USD 754.21 million of liquidity.
- Weaknesses: 5.83x trailing reported net leverage, coupon interest of about USD 158.69 million, 47% customer concentration and a lower free cash flow conversion in 2026.
- Opportunities: a full year of Ruckus earnings, voluntary prepayment of the term loan from free cash flow, and the data center agreement for 2027.
- Threats: distributor destocking, tariff reversal, copper volatility, a failed Ruckus integration and the 2033 maturity concentration.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 25; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_companynewsreleasedatedoct.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C06
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale is average to strong: revenue of USD 2,715.19 million in FY2025 and USD 3,132.61 million over the last twelve months, but a 5% to 15% market share. Competitive advantage is average, resting on breadth and customer relationships rather than documented switching costs. Diversification is average: two segments to 2025 and a regional spread (Americas 66.40% of Q3 revenue), offset by channel concentration. Cost and capex flexibility is average because capex of 5.51% of revenue is not split. Margin stability is average, supported by copper pass-through but flattered by tariff refunds in 2026. Free cash flow stability is average and weakening, with conversion at 24.69% in the nine months of 2026. Access to capital markets is average: the Revolver and notes are in place, but no rating is supplied and 72.40% of principal falls due in 2033. Liquidity is average to strong at USD 754.21 million with little principal due before 2028, and financial policy and governance are average: no sponsor and paused buybacks, but a removed leverage goal. The supports are earnings momentum and liquidity, the constraints are leverage and interest cost, the trend is weaker than FY2025, and the missing data are pro forma EBITDA, interim cash interest and the credit agreements.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C01; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C10
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months demand supports the credit: orders are at record levels entering the fourth quarter, guidance is USD 960 million to USD 980 million of revenue, and the data center agreement adds USD 100 million in 2027. Headwinds are the integration of Ruckus, the unwinding of tariff refunds, floating-rate interest and the sharp rise in non-cash charges that depress reported earnings. Over three to five years the 2028, 2031 and 2033 maturities and the Term Loan B balance of USD 1,734.38 million due in 2033 require leverage to fall, which management's goal of mid-single-digit growth and 25% to 30% incremental margins would support if met.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_companynewsreleasedatedoct.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_companynewsreleasedatedoct.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_bdc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-27_bdc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 23; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05
### Downside scenario

The scenario starts with distributors cutting inventory as demand slows while tariff refunds stop. Revenue falls first because the backlog of USD 567.7 million is short-cycle; gross margin follows because copper costs lag price by about two months; Adjusted EBITDA falls faster than revenue because operating costs and Ruckus integration spending do not adjust quickly. On the trailing base of USD 557.17 million, a 10% fall in Adjusted EBITDA lifts leverage to 5.32x and a 20% fall to 5.99x with no change in net debt, while coupon cover drops to 2.81x. Free cash flow shrinks toward the interest bill, so the Revolver is likely to be drawn first, but USD 754.21 million of liquidity and a nearest maturity in 2028 mean liquidity distress is not the likely outcome inside 24 months; management levers are capex cuts, a continued buyback pause and working capital release. The observable triggers are book-to-bill below 1.00x, margin below 17.0% and Revolver availability moving toward USD 27.0 million.
